title: 2026 SECR post-implementation review and reporting-governance QA controls

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: 2026 post-implementation review of the SECR regulations 2018
RPC Opinion: The Companies (Directors’ Report) and Limited Liability Partnerships (Energy and Carbon Report) Regulations 2018 PIR

facts.source_fact: The SECR framework was introduced in 2019 and replaced the Carbon Reduction Commitment Energy Efficiency Scheme.
facts.expected_handling: Attach framework vintage before comparing historic corporate reporting records.

facts.source_fact: SECR is a mandatory framework requiring large UK businesses in scope to disclose energy use, greenhouse gas emissions and related information in annual reports.
facts.expected_handling: Treat SECR disclosure as an organisational reporting obligation, not a parcel measurement.

facts.source_fact: SECR builds on the 2013 mandatory greenhouse-gas reporting requirements for quoted companies.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve predecessor-framework provenance.

facts.source_fact: SECR extends reporting obligations to large unquoted companies and limited liability partnerships in scope.
facts.expected_handling: Apply entity-type eligibility before assigning reporting expectations.

facts.source_fact: The 2026 review assessed whether SECR achieved its original objectives.
facts.expected_handling: Keep evaluation findings distinct from the underlying legal requirements.

facts.source_fact: The review assessed whether SECR objectives remain appropriate.
facts.expected_handling: Carry review purpose as governance evidence rather than emissions evidence.

facts.source_fact: The review considered unintended consequences of the SECR framework.
facts.expected_handling: Record unintended-consequence findings separately from compliance status.

facts.source_fact: The review considered whether government intervention remains required.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer policy repeal or continuation beyond the published review conclusion.

facts.source_fact: The review considered scope for simplification, improvement or deregulation.
facts.expected_handling: Treat simplification options as review findings, not enacted rules.

facts.source_fact: The review indicates SECR contributed to improved transparency in organisational energy and carbon reporting.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve attribution language and do not convert contribution into a quantified causal effect.

facts.source_fact: The review indicates SECR contributed to improved consistency in company-level energy and carbon reporting.
facts.expected_handling: Keep qualitative consistency findings separate from row-level accuracy scores.

facts.source_fact: The review highlights areas where SECR could be simplified or improved to reduce administrative burden.
facts.expected_handling: Flag this as a prospective refinement area, not a current exemption.

facts.source_fact: The review highlights potential improvements intended to enhance framework effectiveness.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat recommended improvements as already implemented.

facts.source_fact: The 2026 review is intended to inform future work on effectiveness and proportionality of energy and carbon reporting requirements.
facts.expected_handling: Attach publication date and future-policy status.

facts.source_fact: The review considers how SECR fits within the wider landscape of corporate reporting requirements.
facts.expected_handling: Require framework-boundary metadata when comparing SECR with other disclosures.

facts.source_fact: The Regulatory Policy Committee green-rated the PIR as fit for purpose.
facts.expected_handling: Use the RPC rating as review-quality evidence, not as a rating of company emissions data.

facts.source_fact: The RPC found the evidence and analysis sufficient and proportionate for the department's recommendation to amend the framework.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve the distinction between evidence-quality review and policy outcome.

facts.source_fact: The RPC notes that the PIR is underpinned by a substantial mixed-methods evaluation programme.
facts.expected_handling: Record evaluation-method provenance without inventing unreported sample statistics.

facts.source_fact: The RPC describes clearer guidance as one of the proportionate refinements outlined by the PIR.
facts.expected_handling: Treat clearer guidance as a proposed refinement until implemented.

facts.source_fact: The RPC notes proposed improvements to consistency and alignment with other reporting frameworks.
facts.expected_handling: Do not merge metrics from different frameworks without an explicit mapping.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited source fact without broadening its scope.
Attach the applicable organisational, legal or reporting boundary before downstream use.
Attach reference period, publication/update date and implemented-versus-proposed status.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents stale or premature policy use.

guard_patterns.handling: Carry source URL, publisher and evaluation/reporting provenance into derived outputs.
Do not convert organisational reporting governance into parcel-level measured emissions without a separate parcel-binding gate.

generation_rule: CARTESIAN_PRODUCT facts x guard_patterns; control_id={package_id}_{fact_id}_{pattern_id}; each generated row inherits confidence_percent=99 and verification=PASS
